definition: Modest and quiet, not trying to draw attention or seem important.
example: The unassuming farmhouse at the end of the lane held a library of rare maps.
nuance: Humble names an inner attitude, but unassuming describes an outward manner or look, so it also fits places and objects.
prompt: A highly skilled programmer joins a new team at a software company.
options: Though she had won national awards, the unassuming coder rarely mentioned them.
The unassuming coder bragged about her prizes in every team meeting and email.
The unassuming coder fell for the prank because she never suspected a trick.
The unassuming coder questioned every claim, refusing to take anything for granted.
reasons: Keeping quiet about real achievements shows a modest, low-key manner.
Constant boasting is showy, the reverse of a modest manner.
This confuses the word with unsuspecting, which means not expecting a trick.
The word describes modesty, not a literal refusal to make assumptions.

practice.prompt: A tiny restaurant sits between two larger shops on a busy street.
options: The unassuming diner made guests confirm each order twice so no one would guess wrong.
With its faded sign and six tables, the unassuming diner served superb soup.
The unassuming diner hung gold chandeliers and flashing banners to lure crowds.
The unassuming diner had no idea that a famous food critic was eating there.
reasons: Avoiding guesses has nothing to do with a plain, modest appearance.
A plain, easy-to-miss place that hides real quality fits the word well.
Flashy decorations meant to grab attention are the opposite of modest.
Not knowing about a visitor is being unaware, not being modest.
